episodes.204744: Isolated thunderstorms produce strong and gusty outflow winds in northeast Alabama.
episodes.205130: A four corners high pressure advected a high amount of atmospheric moisture into the region. This was day one of an extended push of monsoon moisture that produced heavy rain, localized flooding, strong outflow winds.
episodes.205131: A four corners high pressure advected a high amount of atmospheric moisture into the region. This was day one of an extended push of monsoon moisture that produced heavy rain, localized flooding, strong outflow winds.
episodes.205171: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in a summertime airmass with an isolated severe storm occurring in Thomas county with impacts to trees and power lines. In addition, a very moist airmass and weak steering flow led to flash flooding across portions of southwest Georgia.
episodes.205175: An isolated severe storm over Apalachee bay produced a measured wind gust of 55 knots.  In addition, a waterspout was reported offshore of Saint George Island.
episodes.205505: Two supercell thunderstorms tracked south across the foothills producing damaging hail as large as 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.205971: A front lingering across southeast Georgia with very high moisture across the local area. Weak southwest steering flow around 10 kts, upper divergence and low-level boundaries continued to produce localized flooding rainfall.
episodes.205972: A front lingering across southeast Georgia with very high moisture across the local area. Weak southwest steering flow around 10 kts, upper divergence and low-level boundaries continued to produce localized flooding rainfall.
episodes.206772: An area of storms moved across northwestern Wisconsin and along the South Shore of Lake Superior during the afternoon hours of the 22nd. In addition to some small hail, these storms produced wind gusts to around 45 mph near the shore. Over the open waters of western Lake Superior off the Apostle Islands, a gust to 62 mph was recorded by an iron ore hauling vessel.
episodes.206864: A stalled frontal boundary to the north of the region allowed for low pressure to influence weather over the area.
episodes.206873: Thunderstorms produced gusty winds along the Brevard and Indian River County coasts.
episodes.206877: Early afternoon thunderstorms within westerly sea breeze flow south of a stalled boundary along the northern Gulf Coast produce gusty marine winds in the Sarasota Bay area waters.
episodes.206915: A slow moving cold front encountering an environment displaying deep moisture and moderate instability supported thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.206916: Mid-level energy tracking across the region along with a deep moisture and modest instability residing near a stalled front led to an environment supportive of heavy rainfall across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.206917: Mid-level energy tracking across the region along with a deep moisture and modest instability residing near a stalled front led to an environment supportive of heavy rainfall across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.206952: Scattered air mass thunderstorms developed over the east Tennessee mountains, Cumberland plateau, and central Tennessee valley during the afternoon and evening hours of August 22nd. These storms produced some minor flooding near the Karns and Solway areas.
episodes.206953: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 23rd. The slow moving nature of these storms resulted in heavy rains and notable flooding near the I-26 corridor between Kingsport and Johnson City.
episodes.206977: August 23rd marked the beginning of a push of unusually rich tropical moisture that would plague eastern Utah and western Colorado for the next week. At this point, much of the convective initiation was down to daytime heating on the complex terrain of the region. Heavy rain was not as widespread of a concern as it would be in the following days, but was still possible with stronger storms or in areas of training thunderstorms.
episodes.207067: Storms moved over portions of northeast South Dakota that had really no extra room for moisture from the preceding months of nearly constant rainfall. Thus, this moisture went straight into the Big Sioux and tributaries from the Watertown area down south to Castlewood. The COOP observer in Rauville would record 1.51 inches of rainfall pushing their monthly total up to 5.73 and a 3 month total of 23.32. The Watertown COOP would likewise come up with 1.86 inches, putting the monthly total at 5.85 and 20.1 for the preceding 3 months. Even Castlewood, while only topping out at 0.31 inches, would see their monthly total top out at 4.99 inches with a 3 month total of 22 inches.
episodes.207192: Abundant tropical moisture from a passing tropical wave combines and favorable upper-level conditions from an approaching trough helped promote showers and t-storms during the afternoon of August 23rd. Southeasterly winds steered activity toward northwestern Puerto Rico and from El Yunque to the metro area (El Yunque Streamer).
episodes.207289: Southeasterly flow advected in monsoon moisture, fueling scattered thunderstorms, some of which produced severe winds and dust storm conditions.
